title: The Voynich Manuscript is Written in Natural Language: The Pahlavi Hypothesis
summary: Herrmann argues that the Voynich alphabet is derived from the Iranian Pahlavi script used for Middle Persian: many Voynich glyphs are said to be upside-down Pahlavi letters, others ligatures or additions that resolve Pahlavi's notorious letter ambiguity. He transcribes words from illustration labels and parts of the main text with the proposed letter table and matches several to terms from Zoroastrian cosmology (the Bundahishn) and a Pahlavi dictionary. He explicitly does not attempt a translation.
established: The paper proposes a glyph-to-Pahlavi letter table (Table 1) based on letter-shape comparison, with many Voynich glyphs taken as rotated Pahlavi letters; the evidence is visual similarity plus a few dozen label and text words read with the table, not a statistical or held-out test.

Several transcribed label words, mainly in the astronomical and cosmological sections, are matched to names and terms of Zoroastrian cosmology in the Bundahishn and to Pahlavi dictionary entries; the author calls the transcription tentative and says only a few words have been presented.

The author states there is no evidence that the manuscript was produced in Persia or western India, raises a Black Sea origin as possible, and leaves open whether other idioms (e.g. Parsi Gujarati) are present.

open.question: Does Herrmann's glyph-to-Pahlavi table, frozen as a substitution key, read the hidden pages better than its decoys against a Middle Persian corpus? Openly licensed text: I found no Middle Persian (Pahlavi) transliteration under an explicit open licence at a stable plain-text url; the large digital transliterations (e.g. TITUS, the Bochum MPCD project) do not state cc licences, and E. W. West's 1880-1897 Pahlavi Texts (Sacred Books of the East, public domain) are English translations, not Pahlavi. So no corpus yet; modern Persian (cc-by-sa Wikipedia, many millions of characters) would only be a distant proxy.
open.check: Pin an openly licensed Middle Persian transliteration of 150,000+ characters (kind corpus), then score the frozen table as a key.

open.question: Can a complete phonemic account and translation of more than a few words be given with the proposed table? The author says this needs substantial effort from Pahlavi philologists and is not attempted.
Are the astronomical charts consistent with Bundahishn cosmology rather than Arabic or Latin astronomy, as the author suggests, when compared blind on the scans?
